product: Two clinical oral small molecules: aleniglipron (once-daily selective GLP-1 receptor agonist, Phase 3 for chronic weight management, 45/90/180 mg maintenance doses with 2.5 mg start) and ACCG-2671 (once-weekly oral dual amylin and calcitonin receptor agonist, Phase 1/2a). ACCG-3535 and a GLP-1 plus amylin combination are earlier stage.
demand: Company-cited demand is a 3.0 billion overweight or obese population, under 1% currently on branded anti-obesity medicine, and an over 100 billion dollar total addressable market. Actual evidenced demand is clinical only: no approved product, no product revenue, and multiple Phase 3 readouts outstanding.
pricing_power: Not established; nothing is sold and no price is disclosed. Management positions oral small molecules on convenience, scalable and cost-effective manufacturing and broad global access, implying an access and cost advantage over injectables rather than premium pricing. Payer and reimbursement terms are unproven.
competition: Crowded and fast-moving. Novo Nordisk oral Wegovy and Eli Lilly oral obesity pills reached market in 2026, well ahead of aleniglipron Phase 3 topline in 2H 2028; Zealand and other oral GLP-1 and amylin developers compete. The company itself lists competitive products limiting commercial value as a risk.
team: CEO Raymond Stevens, Ph.D., co-founder of the structure-based platform; CMO Blai Coll, M.D., Ph.D.; CFO Jun Yoon. John Berrios, previously Head of U.S. Sales Strategy and Innovation for Obesity and Diabetes at Novo Nordisk, was appointed Chief Commercial Officer in 2026. About 281 employees.
market_strategy: Build a wholly owned portfolio of oral small-molecule chronic weight management medicines covering monotherapy, maintenance after injectables and combinations, differentiated by convenience, scalability, cost and broad global access, targeting the over 100 billion dollar obesity market. Wholly owned, no partnered economics disclosed.
bull: 2026-09-08 8-K: ACCG-2671 Phase 1 SAD showed no SAEs, up to 3.3% weight loss after one 10 mg dose, CTX-1 down ~60%; aleniglipron ACCESS 72-week OLE reached 16.2% weight loss with no plateau and under 5% discontinuations, funded by $1.3B cash.
bear: Pre-revenue; Phase 3 topline not due until 2H 2028. Shares fell ~14.7% on the 2026-09-08 data, closed 36.02 on 2026-09-24 versus a 94.90 52-week high, 63-day momentum -19%, two sell ratings, and cash fell to $1.3B from $1.5B.
falsifier: ACCG-2671 MAD topline, due 1H 2027, showing dose-limiting GI discontinuations or no meaningful weight loss versus the 3.3% single-dose SAD signal.

web_demand_price_volume_mix: None of the four: Structure is pre-revenue with no approved product, so there is no demand, price, volume or mix to decompose. What moves it is clinical milestones and financing. Management frames size of opportunity instead (3.0 billion overweight or obese people, less than 1% treated, over 100 billion dollar market).
web_suppliers: Not found. No suppliers are named. The 2026-09-08 presentation risk disclosure states reliance on third parties including clinical research organizations, manufacturers, suppliers and collaborators over which it may not have full control. No disclosed capacity constraint or supplier concentration.
web_customers: Not found. Structure has no approved product and no customers. Prospective demand is patients, prescribers and payers. The Phase 3 ACCOMPLISH-1 and ACCOMPLISH-2 enroll up to 3,600 and 1,100 trial participants, which are study subjects rather than customers.
web_who_loses: Injectable GLP-1 incumbents Novo Nordisk (Wegovy) and Eli Lilly (Zepbound) and the oral obesity pills both launched in 2026, if a cheaper, scalable oral wins share. Peptide API makers and injection-device suppliers lose if small-molecule orals displace peptides, as management explicitly argues.
web_contradicting_evidence: Shares fell about 14.7% on 2026-09-08 despite the quote positive data, and closed 36.02 on 2026-09-24 versus a 52-week high of 94.90, roughly a 62% drawdown; 63-day momentum is negative 19%. Two sell ratings exist. ACCG-2671 caused dose-related GI events (nausea 4 of 5 at 5 mg, 6 of 6 at 10 mg). Phase 3 topline is not due until 2H 2028 and Q2 EPS missed consensus by 0.10.
web_if_management_right: ACCG-2671 MAD topline in 1H 2027 and the Q4 2026 body-composition, T2DM and SWITCH datasets confirm a differentiated oral profile. ACCOMPLISH Phase 3 validates 45-180 mg dosing and delivers 2H 2028 topline, while ACCG-3535 and the GLP-1 plus amylin combination advance, funded by 1.3 billion dollars of cash through 2028.
web_if_management_wrong: Tolerability or efficacy disappoints, discontinuations rise, or Novo and Lilly oral incumbents lock payer access and manufacturing scale years earlier. Because Phase 3 topline is not due until 2H 2028, value depends on financing well before revenue; cash fell to 1.3 billion dollars at 2026-06-30 from 1.5 billion at 2026-03-31, so dilution or a partnership is the first thing to break.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Small-molecule API makers and CDMOs able to scale oral GLP-1 and amylin chemistry; the CROs and clinical sites running the roughly 4,700-patient Phase 3 and five ACCG-2671 MAD cohorts; obesity diagnostics, biomarker and bone-health labs; and pharmacies, telehealth and weight-management platforms that gain a cheaper oral option.
